∠B + 30◦ . Prove that ∠A + ∠COP < 90◦ .

Solution 1. Let α = ∠CAB, β = ∠ABC, γ = ∠BCA, and δ = ∠COP . Let K
and Q be the reflections of A and P , respectively, across the perpendicular bisector of
BC. Let R denote the circumradius of 4ABC. Then OA = OB = OC = OK = R.
Furthermore, we have QP = KA because KQP A is a rectangle. Now note that
∠AOK = ∠AOB − ∠KOB = ∠AOB − ∠AOC = 2γ − 2β ≥ 60◦ .

It follows from this and from OA = OK = R that KA ≥ R and QP ≥ R. Therefore,
using the Triangle Inequality, we have OP + R = OQ + OC > QC = QP + P C ≥
R + P C. It follows that OP > P C, and hence in 4COP , ∠P CO > δ. Now since
α = 12 ∠BOC = 12 (180◦ − 2∠P CO) = 90◦ − ∠P CO, it indeed follows that α + δ < 90◦ .

that 41 > sin α sin β cos γ.

It follows that δ < ∠OBC = 90◦ − α or α + δ < 90◦ .
